howDoI.q: How do I make a key play a sound?
How do I make my hero say a line out loud?
How do I make a block talk when it is touched?
How do I get two blocks to say different things?
How do I keep a voice from being cut off at the door?
How do I use a recording of my own voice?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Out Loud is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first, with a Sound Blaster set up so the voices play. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Enter makes Kit say hello. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you. The voices are hums made in code, not recordings of anyone.

pages.head: Level 1: Say Hello
pages.html:
Level 1: Say Hello

PRESS ENTER AND KIT SAYS HELLO comes first. Press Enter and Kit throws his arms up and says it. A KEY CAN PLAY A SOUND. THIS ONE PLAYS A VOICE FILE comes next, then three coins. PRESS IT AGAIN AND THE VOICE STARTS OVER stands before three more coins and the door: press Enter while Kit is still talking and the hello begins again from the start.

There are six coins, ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The key. Open the character in the Character tab and pick the cheer sequence. Its Key is Enter. In the Starters this sequence has no key; here it was given one, so it plays when you press Enter.
  • The sound. The same sequence has a Sound of 13. A sequence plays its sound number as it starts.
  • The voice. Open vo1.snd in the Sounds tab and look at sound 13. It has two halves: a short PC speaker tune for a game with no sound card, and a Sound Blaster file, HELLO.VOC. With a Sound Blaster the game plays the file.
  • One at a time. Starting a voice stops the one that is playing, which is why a second Enter begins the hello again.

pages.head: Level 2: Two Speakers
pages.html:
Level 2: Two Speakers

WALK INTO A SPEAKER AND IT TALKS comes first. ITS COUNTER GOES UP, SO IT PLAYS THE UP VOICE stands before the first loudspeaker: walk into it and it says a welcome, once. THIS COUNTER GOES DOWN: THE OTHER VOICE stands before the second loudspeaker, which has a lower voice. Each speaker turns into a quiet one after it speaks.

There are seven coins, ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The first speaker. Open vo.bbl in the Blocks tab and pick speaker. It is not solid. Its Touch tab adds 1 to counter 22, and its Becomes block is hush, the same speaker without its sound waves.
  • Why that makes a voice. When a touch makes a counter go up, Game-Maker plays sound 7. Open vo2.snd and sound 7 names WELCOME.VOC.
  • The second speaker. Pick lower. It takes 1 from counter 23, and Game-Maker plays sound 8, which in this level's sound set is DEEPER.VOC. The block does not choose a clip. The direction its counter moves does.
  • Counters 22 and 23. The character starts with one in hand on each, so that taking one away is allowed; a counter from 20 up refuses a touch that would take it to zero or less.

pages.head: Level 3: Let It Finish
pages.html:
Level 3: Let It Finish

A NEW SCENE CUTS A VOICE OFF comes first. Further on a loudspeaker stands with a long goodbye. THE DOOR IS FAR ENOUGH FOR THE WHOLE LINE stands past it. From the speaker to the door is a walk of twenty blocks, which takes more than twice as long as the line does, so the whole goodbye plays before the next scene starts.

There are nine coins, ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • The speaker. It is the same speaker block as level 2, but this level uses vo3.snd, where sound 7 names BYE.VOC instead. A level picks its sound set, so one block can say different things in different levels.
  • The cut. When the game goes to another scene it frees the voice that is playing, and the new scene may start another. So the last line of a level has to finish first. Kit walks about three and a half blocks a second, so twenty blocks takes him over five seconds, and the goodbye lasts about two and a half.
  • Do the sum. Divide the clip's length by how fast the hero moves to know how far the speaker must stand from the door. The Level check does not do this for you.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot play two voices at once. A new voice stops the old one. Press Enter over a speaker and you hear the hello and lose the rest of the welcome.
  • A block cannot choose its clip. Only the counter that changes does, and a sound set has one clip for "a counter went up" and one for "a counter went down", shared by every block in the level. For more voices, use a sound set per level or a character move with a sound number of its own.
  • A text page or an animation cannot play a voice. Only a level plays sounds. A clip still playing when a scene changes is cut off.
  • It needs a Sound Blaster. With no card, the game plays the PC speaker tune for the same sound.
  • A clip is read whole into memory when it starts. The byte count is 16 bits, so keep a clip under 64 KB, which is about five seconds at 11 kHz.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Record a line of your own, save it as 8-bit mono at 11 kHz in a .voc file named HELLO.VOC, and press Enter.
  • Change which key says hello on the cheer sequence.
  • Swap WELCOME and DEEPER in vo2.snd.
  • Move the last speaker close to the door and listen to the goodbye get cut off.
  • Give a speaker a second touch that turns it into another speaker with the other voice.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
